sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the observed binary-instrument experiment with fixed \(\pi_z>0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Instrument arms have positive probabilities; treatment overlap outside \([p_0,p_1]\) is not imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are estimated by armwise empirical proportions and projected onto \(\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E\) only for the certified regular branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Uniformly sharp rank-similar counterfactual-average bounds rely on full complier support.
Aumann-expectation identification regions admit Hausdorff-consistent estimation and set-valued limit theory.
Criterion-minimizer identified sets admit Hausdorff-rate and confidence-region analysis.
Test inversion can cover an entire identified set uniformly under stated conditions.
Ordinary-bootstrap validity under Gaussian limits is equivalent to full Hadamard differentiability.
Calibrated projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions in moment-inequality models.
Sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds can have nonstandard limits and ordinary-bootstrap failure.
Categorical instrumental-variable compatibility and confidence inversion reduce to finite convex programs.
Discrete structural instrumental-variable functions are generally set identified and support sensitive.

body.tldr: A binary instrument identifies complier outcome distributions but policies below \(p_0\) and above \(p_1\) require extrapolation. Under exactly Marx's existential rank similarity and a fixed finite ordered outcome alphabet, the sharp simultaneous policy-mean set is a finite nonconvex union of common-rank path images, each attained by one law. The comparison to Marx is confined to this finite-alphabet extension in the missing-complier-support direction, and the observable monotonicity inequalities are derived from the latent model. Path survival gives the exact Hausdorff continuity frontier and a centered local Lipschitz bound. A legal three-outcome contiguous submodel proves that globally honest metric procedures cannot shrink uniformly. A terminating finite algorithm computes the multinomial outer set, the set-of-sets image, and their exact Hausdorff radii; finite-sample coverage is the direct inversion corollary. The paper's open statistical kernel is recovery of the complete projected Hausdorff-loss germ on every certified continuous sampling face.

project_justification.gap: Marx's full-support condition makes rank-similar groupwise extrema jointly attainable. Within the fixed finite-alphabet setting, allowing missing complier support leaves no published sharp joint policy-grid set, no stability criterion for disappearing common-rank couplings, and no finite procedure computing Hausdorff radii for the resulting set-of-sets inversion.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes convert existential common ranks into finitely many ordered chains, but the resulting set is a law-dependent nonconvex union rather than one convex program or one smooth projection.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the observable compatibility inequalities from the maintained latent model and supplies a sharp path-union representation, finite exclusion certificates, an if-and-only-if continuity frontier, a contiguous impossibility theorem, a terminating exact inversion-and-radius algorithm, the accompanying finite-sample coverage corollary, and a concrete full-loss germ handle for the remaining regular-calibration question.

body.related_work: Marx (2024) is the direct substantive anchor: Proposition 5 obtains uniformly sharp rank-similar policy bounds under full complier support, and footnote 29 identifies the construction that fails without it. The path theorem addresses that missing-support direction for a fixed finite outcome alphabet, so the comparison is directional rather than a model-class inclusion. Imbens and Rubin (1997) give the principal-stratum interpretation underlying the observable monotonicity inequalities; here those inequalities are derived as compatibility checks. Chesher (2010), Torgovitsky (2019), and Han and Yang (2024) show how discrete structural restrictions can be encoded by finite feasibility or linear programs; they inform the allocation representation but do not impose one common ordered rank across every latent-index bin. Beresteanu and Molinari (2008) and Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) provide regular Hausdorff theory for different set-valued substrates; the survival theorem addresses law-dependent component death in a nonconvex union. Romano and Shaikh (2010) motivate the coverage corollary through general identified-set inversion. Song et al. (2026) informs the finite categorical feasibility layer, while the algorithm theorem adds common-parameter nonconvex unions and exact outer-set and hyperspace Hausdorff radii. Fang and Santos (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Fan and Park (2010) motivate the active-germ problem, but none proves recovery of the complete projected Hausdorff-loss partition on structural-zero faces.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact bottleneck is not generic directional differentiation. The full projected Hausdorff loss can change affine pieces while every path domain remains unchanged. A valid proof must compile boundary and value-intercept forms, include model projection, snap their diagonal zero sets, and verify the same homogeneous germ on all relative tangent faces. A path-domain-only bootstrap is insufficient.
body.honest_scope: The path representation is scoped to a fixed finite outcome alphabet and the missing-complier-support direction relative to Marx's full-support result; the comparison is not a model-class inclusion. The finite survival criterion, centered Lipschitz implication, three-outcome discontinuity, impossibility argument, and exact finite inversion-and-radius algorithm are theorem targets with concrete proof architectures. The inequalities \(c_0\ge0\) and \(c_1\ge0\) are derived observed-law compatibility checks, not maintained assumptions. Simultaneous coverage is a direct corollary of observed-law coverage and the inversion definitions, not a headline theorem, and no finite-sample optimality is claimed. Pairwise-neighborhood Lipschitz continuity, a globally continuous derivative, and globally shrinking honest Hausdorff inference are not claimed. The general active-stratum calibration is explicitly open; only the interior one-path folded-normal case is posed as a closed benchmark. Under full complier support the coordinate projections must reduce to Marx's Proposition 5, and for \(K=2\) only the two monotone paths remain.
